gaps.sentence: He repaired the car ___ engine had failed.
gaps.hint: the engine belongs to the car
gaps.explanation: 'Whose engine' means 'the car's engine', showing possession even with objects.

gaps.sentence: It was Marie Curie ___ discoveries changed modern medicine.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose discoveries' means 'Marie Curie's discoveries'; 'who's' would mean 'who is'.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: The shower suddenly stopped working, ___ meant we had to call a plumber.
gaps.hint: refers back to the whole event
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to the whole preceding clause; 'what' cannot introduce this kind of clause after a comma.

gaps.sentence: They chose a guide on ___ they could rely completely.
gaps.hint: rely on somebody — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: After the preposition 'on', the person takes 'whom'; 'which' is only for things.

gaps.sentence: Nobody explained the reason ___ the flight was cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Why' introduces the cause after 'the reason'; it means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: All ___ I want is a quiet weekend at home.
gaps.explanation: After 'all' the relative pronoun is 'that' (often omitted); 'all what' is always wrong.

gaps.sentence: I'll never forget the day ___ we first met.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'on which' after time nouns like day, year and moment.
